actual_scope: For the pinned helper-462 matcher, exhibit a zero-swap word with exactly one scale of coefficient -16 and strictly fewer than 29 shears. The witness has 26 shears. The same column-ordered repair branch recorded by open PR #7030 still has 29, and the merged elimination of #6954 still has 53. rank(D^{-1} S - I) = 8 is rechecked and is not improved. Twenty-six is not claimed to be minimal. No P2 bill and no new kappa.
scope_change_reason: Handoff comment 19137812 asks for one literal stock/role/route generator. Merged PR #6954 gives a 53-shear one-scale word, and open PR #7030 gives a 29-shear one-scale word and leaves lengths 9 through 28 open. This package answers only that length question, by an explicit 26-shear word. It does not audit supplier admission, price P2 tariffs, raise the rank lower bound, or search words with two or more scales.
bottleneck_link: The route ledger is one charged part of the missing physical generator. Open PR #7030 lowered the recorded one-scale shear count from 53 to 29 and left 9 through 28 open. An explicit 26-shear word with the same scale by -16 shows that 29 is not the one-scale length. The rechecked rank bound of 8 still leaves 9 through 25 open. Neither number is a tariff or a new kappa.
stop_rule: Stop after the explicit 26-shear word, the checked replacement of one 4-shear block by the 3-shear signed exchange, the two-shear diagonal identity, and the recheck that the column-ordered repair branch still has length 29 and that rank(D^{-1} S - I) = 8. Do not search every rational word of length at most 25, raise the rank bound, price P2 tariffs, or change the selected frontier.
evidence: Exact rational product of the frozen 0-swap, 1-scale, 26-shear word equals the pinned matcher, and so does the elementary-matrix product. The first four shears multiply to the same matrix as the balanced scale of unit -1 on rows 0 and 6. Shears 18 through 20 multiply to the same matrix as an explicit four-shear block, and restoring that block gives a 27-shear word for the same matrix. Shears 7 through 10 have two diagonal entries different from 1; every product of two shears changes at most one diagonal entry, by an exhaustive polynomial identity on all positions. The column-ordered repair branch on D^{-1} S still has 29 shears, and the merged elimination still has 53. rank(D^{-1} S - I) = 8 for every scale row. Dropping any letter, replacing the scale by -8 or +16, or adding 1 to the first shear misses S.

open_questions.question: Is there a zero-swap word with exactly one scale of coefficient -16 and fewer than 26 shears?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Twenty-six is the length of this witness and an upper bound. The rechecked rank bound is 8, so the integers 9 through 25 remain open.
open_questions.first_step: Keep one scale of coefficient -16. Shears 7 through 10 act on rows 0, 1 and 3 and are not a product of two shears. Decide whether that block is a product of three shears, and whether splicing the shorter block back into this word still multiplies to the matcher.
open_questions.blocked_by: Rational shear coefficients make the set of words of length at most 25 infinite. The two-shear diagonal identity blocks only a two-shear replacement of that one block.

open_questions.question: Can a third row shorten the opening balanced scale of unit -1 on rows 0 and 6?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Those four shears multiply to diag(-1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, -1, 1). Inside the two rows, two shears cannot change both diagonal entries. A helper row could still make the whole word shorter.
open_questions.first_step: Factor diag(-1, -1, 1) as a product of elementary shears in a three-dimensional coordinate subspace, then count whether embedding that factorization into the 26-shear word reduces the length.
open_questions.blocked_by: A factorization that uses a third row has to restore that row. This package does not enumerate three-shear words for diag(-1, -1, 1).
